title: Nexo Connect connector manifest
description: What a connector may do, checked before a version is stored: its triggers, the hosts it calls, the names of its secrets, the Nexo objects it reads and writes, and whether it writes to the other system. Names repeated in a list are refused.

triggers.description: What starts a run: up to five, any mix of cron, webhook and Nexo event

type.description: Runs on a schedule, every everyMinutes minutes
Runs when the other system calls the connector's signed webhook
Runs when a Nexo event happens

event.description: Nexo event that starts a run; the run input carries the event and the record id

hosts.description: Domains the code calls with ctx.http and ctx.soap, over https; a new one waits for a yes before a rehearsal

items.description: Domain the connector may call over https, without scheme, port or path

sftp.description: SFTP servers the connector reads files from, through the gateway

host.description: Domain of the SFTP server, without scheme, port or path

port.description: Port of the SFTP server (22 is the usual one)

hostKey.description: Fingerprint of the server key (SHA256:..., as ssh-keyscan | ssh-keygen -lf - prints it); any other key is refused

email.description: Spreadsheets arriving by e-mail at the connector's own address, read with ctx.email; only from these senders

senders.description: Who may send the files: an address (relatorios@erp.com.br) or a whole domain (@erp.com.br); mail from anyone else is dropped

drive.description: Spreadsheets in Google Drive folders of the company's Google Workspace, read with ctx.drive through the Nexo's delegation

account.description: E-mail of the company's person whose Google Workspace account reads the folders (a Nexo user of the company): the Nexo's delegation reads Drive as this account

folders.description: Google Drive folders the connector reads: the folder link (drive.google.com/drive/folders/...) or its id

secrets.description: Secrets the code reads with ctx.secret(name): a person fills the value in, it never sits in the code

name.description: Name the code uses to reference the secret

label.description: What the person fills in, in Portuguese

help.description: Where the person finds the value in the other system

writes.description: Nexo objects and fields the connector writes

items.description: Native field (camelCase) or custom property as property:<key>

controlledFields.description: Fields the other system owns: the Nexo shows where they come from and warns before a manual edit

items.description: Native field (camelCase) or custom property as property:<key>

externalWrites.description: Whether the connector writes into the other system

agents.description: Local agents inside the customer's network and what the connector reaches through each: internal APIs and databases

agentId.description: Id of the local agent (Integrações › Agente local); the gateway sends these calls down its tunnel

http.description: APIs inside the customer's network, called with ctx.http

host.description: Host inside the customer's network, as the agent's machine resolves it: a name, a domain or an IPv4

tls.description: true when the API is https, false when it is plain http inside the network

name.description: How the code names this database in ctx.db.query({ database })

host.description: Host inside the customer's network, as the agent's machine resolves it: a name, a domain or an IPv4

port.description: Port of the database (1433 SQL Server, 1521 Oracle, 3050 Firebird)

database.description: The database as the server knows it: SQL Server database name, Oracle service name, Firebird path or alias

username.description: Name of the secret with the read-only database user

password.description: Name of the secret with its password

oauth.description: Whether the code calls the other system with the OAuth token the person authorized: ctx.secret("OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN"), renewed by the gateway
